_why: Step 3.6's value is carried by its SHORT lists, and the short list is the fragile one. Every mutant here widens the step exactly the way a future reader's instinct will: drop the scope limit from the heading, soften the fail-closed predicate, or delete one never-list entry that looks locally safe. None of them break a behaviour a normal test could see — the step is guidance, so the guidance is what gets pinned, and a deleted sentence is invisible until the resume it would have stopped.

mutations.name: scope-limit-dropped-from-the-heading
mutations._mechanism: `and only that` is the whole contract. Without it the heading reads as 'resolve what is resolvable', which is the blanket rule the step exists to refuse — and a reader who never reaches the never-list has already been told the wrong thing.
mutations.find: ### Step 3.6: Resolve what is mechanically resolvable — and only that

mutations.name: fail-closed-predicate-softened
mutations._mechanism: Delete the line that distinguishes an unevaluable gate from a passing one. This repo has shipped that exact conflation twice — `find` under rtk refusing to run and reading as 'nothing is claimed', and an unreadable worktree comment reading as empty and clobbering a human's note. Without the line, a gate that errors reads as a green light.
mutations.find:
**"I could not check" and "the check said yes" must never
take the same branch.**

mutations.name: fast-forwardable-sibling-no-longer-refused-by-name
mutations._mechanism: The most tempting entry in the never-list, and the one that looks cleanest: no divergence, no uncommitted work, a pure fast-forward. Removing the explicit clause leaves only the general 'another worktree' rule, which a reader will reason their way past — the cost is not to git, it is that another session's files change under a running agent.
mutations.find:
including a sibling branch that is cleanly
  fast-forwardable.

mutations.name: allowlist-no-longer-declared-closed
mutations._mechanism: Drop `Nothing outside it.` and the ban on extending the list in the moment. The entries all survive, so the step still looks correct — but the failure mode was never a wrong entry, it was growth: each new case is argued individually and looks safe, and the step becomes the blanket rule one row at a time.

mutations.name: empty-resolved-block-may-be-omitted
mutations._mechanism: Let a resume that repaired nothing print no Resolved block. Absence then reads as 'this resume does not do repairs', the next reader stops expecting them, and a step that silently did nothing is indistinguishable from one that was never run.
mutations.find:
If Step 3.6 resolved nothing, say
`**Resolved:** none` rather than omitting the block;
mutations.replace: If Step 3.6 resolved nothing, omit the block;
